_note: Victorian overrides. Every constant not listed here is taken from data/constants.json unchanged: hot water demand, efficiencies, COP, installed costs (DCCEEW RIS Table 20 is national), rebate (0) and deal parameters.

EF_electricity_VIC_kgCO2e_per_kWh.source: DCCEEW, 'Australian National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2026', August 2026, Table 1, 'Victoria': scope 2 = 0.74, scope 3 = 0.11.

EF_gas_VIC_kgCO2e_per_MJ.source: DCCEEW, 'Australian National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2026'. Table 5, 'Natural gas distributed in a pipeline', scope 1 = 51.53 kg CO2-e/GJ. Table 6, 'Victoria', scope 3 = 4.0 kg CO2-e/GJ.
EF_gas_VIC_kgCO2e_per_MJ.note: UNIT TRAP: per MJ, not per GJ. 55.53 / 1000 = 0.05553.

tariffs.source: AER Consumer Data Right, Energy Product Reference Data API. AGL Residential Standing Offer, time of use with controlled load, and AGL Residential Standing Offer gas. Raw responses in data/cdr_raw/vic/.
tariffs.timeOfUse: Two rates: $0.3233/kWh from 15:00 to 21:00 every day, $0.1928/kWh at all other times. The heat pump is assumed to run outside 15:00 to 21:00 on a timer, as the NSW model assumes it runs off-peak.
tariffs.gasBlockPeriod: AGL publishes Victorian gas blocks per two-month billing period (P2M): 1,644 MJ then 1,314 MJ. We convert to daily blocks by dividing by 60, which reproduces EnergyAustralia's daily (P1D) standing offer blocks on the same AGN network exactly: 27.4 and 21.9 MJ/day (data/cdr_raw/vic/detail_TRU796856SR_at_VEC.json).
tariffs.gst: CDR unit prices are stored the same way for both states, so NSW and VIC figures are on the same basis.

finding: Victoria's grid is dirtier than NSW's (0.85 vs 0.67 kg CO2-e/kWh) and its gas supply chain is cleaner (scope 3 of 4.0 vs 13.1 kg CO2-e/GJ), so the same switch abates less in Victoria. That is a real result of the factors, not an error.
